title: Most news apps try to guess what you like by watching what you click.
body:
That approach creates a feedback loop. If you click on a sensational headline once, the algorithm decides that is all you want to see. It is a trap that narrows your worldview rather than expanding it.

At Headlinne, we made a deliberate engineering choice to avoid this trap. Instead of prioritizing clicks, our system is built to prioritize context and variety. We treat your feed like a balanced diet. If you read a piece on tech policy, we do not just serve you ten more articles on the same topic. We ensure you see a mix of perspectives so you get the full picture, not just the echo chamber.

Building an AI that understands nuance is harder than building one that chases engagement. It requires us to teach the model to value information quality over raw attention metrics. It is a slower way to build, but it is the only way to build trust.

We believe technology should serve your curiosity, not exploit your impulses.
cta: You can see how this approach feels in practice at HEADLINNE.com.
